title: Riding in the Rust engine: original quad, rider and chase camera
summary: The shared Rust engine (one codebase for web and macOS/Windows/Linux) now rides ENV01 Freeride on the default original quad with the male rider. It runs the recovered physics at 60 Hz in the same order as the JS game, with wrecks and recovery, keyboard and gamepad input on default bindings, and the chase camera including the JS game's portrait framing for phones. Quad and rider use their original textures with the browser's vehicle lighting and fog. PR #182 (merge 5bab20e) is merged and live: https://furyremastered.com/deployment.json reports 5bab20e, so the preview page https://furyremastered.com/engine.html is publicly deployed. play.html remains the main JS game.
details: Replay comparison: a new tool runs one scripted control sequence through the JS game, the Rust browser build and the Rust native build and compares every step. 600 steps agree within 0.00024 ft. A 930-step script with two wrecks matches the JS game exactly. Browser and native Rust end within 0.00002 ft of each other.
Rendering comparison: the quad and rider screen area differs from the JS game by about 1.3/255 mean (landscape) and about 2/255 (portrait).

Cost: the native physics step takes 0.04 ms on an Apple M4. The user's iPhone ran the earlier terrain-only preview at a steady 61 fps with 1.3 ms CPU per frame; this riding build has not been re-measured there. The wasm is 1.05 MB brotli.

Screenshot: I inspected the Rust browser frame and the JS frame from the same moment. The quad, rider, number plate, terrain and fog match closely. The Rust frame has no trees, fence or foreground bush because scenery is still in progress separately.
limitation: No sky, trees, props or other scenery yet (in progress separately), no audio, HUD, minimap, menus or touch controls, so phones can view but not ride yet. No effects, motorcycles, races or multiplayer. Physical controllers are untested. The JS game remains the playable product; this is a preview of the shared engine.
caption: Rust engine in the browser: ENV01 Freeride, original quad with the male rider, chase camera. Compared with the JS game at the same moment, the Rust frame lacks the sky, trees, fence and bush that the JS frame shows.
